In Egypt, Pharaoh summons his chartummim to interpret his dreams (Gen 41:8, 24) and to replicate Moses' signs (Exod 7:11, 22; 8:3 [Eng. 8:7]). They manage to match the first two plagues but fail at the gnats, conceding 'this is the finger of God' (Exod 8:14-15 [Eng. 8:18-19]), and are themselves afflicted with boils (Exod 9:11). In Daniel, the same term reappears for the Babylonian court magicians whom Daniel outperforms tenfold (Dan 1:20; 2:2). The word likely derives from Egyptian hry-tp ('chief lector-priest'). Spanish 'magos' and English 'magicians' are standard renderings."
